title: Korea Arrival Checklist for Travelers & Digital Nomads (2026)

phases.title: Before You Fly
phases.description: Prep before you board. Some app features lock behind a Korean phone number — load everything while you still have home WiFi.

items.label: Choose your entry path: B-2 visa-free or F-1-D Digital Nomad Visa
items.description: B-2 visa-free covers 106+ countries for up to 90 days. F-1-D gives up to 2 years but requires ₩88M+ (~$64K) annual income proof. Apply at your nearest Korean embassy 2–4 weeks before departure.
tips: F-1-D applicants: do not book non-refundable flights until your visa clears. Processing takes 2–4 weeks and embassies do not rush.

items.label: Check K-ETA requirement (B-2 travelers)
items.description: K-ETA may be required for B-2 visa-free travelers. Check the current eligible country list before departure.
warnings: Requirements change — verify on the official K-ETA site before every trip, not just once.

items.label: Download KakaoTalk, Naver Map, and Papago
items.description: Three essential apps before you board:
tips: KakaoTalk: messaging — Korea runs on this, not WhatsApp or Telegram
Naver Map: Korean transit routing and walking directions, better than Google Maps
Papago: Naver's translator, beats Google Translate for Korean ↔ English
Download while on home WiFi — some features lock behind a Korean phone number after arrival

items.label: Pre-buy a Korean eSIM or plan for airport SIM pickup
items.description: Options: Airalo or eSIMDB for eSIM before departure, or pick up a SIM at Incheon arrival hall. You will upgrade to a Korean postpaid number later, but you need data from minute one.

items.label: Pack all required documents
tips: Passport (6+ months validity)
Visa approval letter (if F-1-D)
Insurance documents
Accommodation address written in Korean (한글)
2 passport photos (3.5×4.5cm, white background — Korean standard, NOT US size)
warnings: Korean passport photo size is 3.5×4.5cm. US standard (2×2 in) is a different size — bring Korean-format photos.

items.label: Bring ₩300,000–500,000 ($230–385) in cash
items.description: Korea is technically 80%+ cashless, but that means Korean payment methods. Your foreign card will be rejected at small restaurants, kiosks, street food stalls, and delivery apps. Cash is essential backup.
warnings: Apple Pay launched March 2023 with Hyundai Card only — do not count on it working.
Samsung Pay requires a Korean phone and Korean bank card — not available until after ARC + bank setup.

phases.title: Day 1: Incheon Airport
phases.description: After clearing customs, hit the arrivals hall in this order. Do not skip the WOWPASS step.

items.label: Get a tourist SIM at Incheon
items.description: KT or LG U+ counters in the arrivals hall. 30-day data SIM runs ₩33,000–55,000. Or activate your pre-purchased eSIM now.

items.label: Get a WOWPASS card (₩6,000)
items.description: WOWPASS works as a prepaid payment card (accepted anywhere T-money or credit cards work), a transit card, and a foreign currency exchange machine. Card costs ₩6,000. Load with cash or your foreign card at WOWPASS kiosks. Better exchange rates than airport currency counters.
tips: This is your main card for the first week. Works at most shops and all transit.
Way better exchange rates than the airport currency counters.

items.label: Take AREX or limousine bus to Seoul
items.description: WOWPASS and T-money work on all options:
tips: AREX All-Stop: ₩4,750, ~60 min to Seoul Station
AREX Express: ₩11,000, ~43 min (more space for luggage)
Limousine Bus: ₩15,000–18,000, 60–90 min door-to-door to major areas

phases.title: Days 1–2: Settle In
phases.description: Get oriented. Learn your neighborhood before diving into admin tasks.

items.label: Walk your neighborhood and find key spots
items.description: Find the nearest subway station (memorize the exit number — Korean addresses are exit-number-dependent), convenience store (CU, GS25), pharmacy (약국), and a few restaurants.

items.label: Set up KakaoTalk with your tourist SIM number
items.description: KakaoTalk is your primary communication channel in Korea. Set it up now — landlords, coworkers, and everyone else will contact you here, not via SMS or email.
warnings: KakaoTaxi and delivery apps (Baemin, Coupang Eats) require Korean 본인인증 (identity verification tied to a postpaid plan). These are NOT available until after the postpaid upgrade in Days 5+. Flag taxis on the street for now.

items.label: Set up your first-week payment stack
items.description: Three layers to cover every situation:
tips: WOWPASS: your main card — works at most shops and all transit
Cash ₩50,000–100,000: for small restaurants, traditional markets, and Korean-card-only spots
T-money: backup transit card (cash recharge at any convenience store)
Large chains and department stores usually accept foreign cards; small spots often don't

items.label: Test accommodation WiFi
items.description: Korea's standard is 1 Gbps fiber. If you are getting under 100 Mbps consistently, something is wrong with the setup, not the country. Ask your host to check.

phases.title: Days 2–5: ARC + Phone
phases.description: Korea has a strict dependency chain: ARC → phone → bank. Each step unlocks the next. Do not skip or reorder.

items.label: Apply for ARC (Alien Registration Card) at immigration office
items.description: Apply at the immigration office (출입국사무소). For F-1-D visa holders, apply within 7 days of arrival. For B-2 or others, within 90 days. The physical card takes 2–3 weeks, but Mobile ARC activates same-day and banks accept the digital version.
tips: Activate Mobile ARC immediately after applying — it is accepted by banks for account opening.
Full step-by-step is in the ARC → Phone → Bank guide.
items.linkLabel: ARC → Phone → Bank: Breaking Korea's Catch-22
warnings: F-1-D visa holders must apply within 7 days of arrival — do not delay.
ARC is required before you can get a postpaid phone plan or open a bank account.

items.label: Activate Mobile ARC same-day
items.description: After submitting your ARC application, activate the Mobile ARC (디지털 외국인등록증) on your phone. Banks accept this digital version — you do not need to wait for the physical card.

phases.title: Days 5+: Bank + Postpaid Unlock
phases.description: With ARC in hand, you can open a bank account and upgrade to postpaid. The postpaid phone is the real key to living in Korea — it unlocks nearly every Korean app and service.

items.label: Open a Korean bank account (Hana, Shinhan, or KB Kookmin)
items.description: With ARC (or Mobile ARC) and a prepaid SIM, walk into Hana Bank, Shinhan, or KB Kookmin. Staff accept prepaid SIM numbers at this stage.
tips: Hana Bank and Shinhan are generally the most foreigner-friendly.
Bring your passport, ARC (or Mobile ARC), and prepaid SIM.

items.label: Upgrade to a postpaid phone plan (KT, SKT, or LG U+)
items.description: Requires ARC + Korean bank account. This single upgrade unlocks:
tips: Kakao Pay, Naver Pay, Samsung Pay
KakaoTaxi (finally)
Baemin and Coupang Eats delivery
Full internet banking features
Most Korean apps that require 본인인증 (identity verification)
warnings: Do this AFTER opening a bank account — postpaid plans require Korean bank payment setup.

items.label: Set up Kakao Pay, Naver Pay, or Samsung Pay
items.description: With a postpaid plan and Korean bank account, you can now register for Korean mobile payment apps. Samsung Pay is dominant, but all three are widely accepted.
tips: Samsung Pay requires a Samsung device.
Kakao Pay and Naver Pay work on any smartphone.

items.label: Set up Baemin or Coupang Eats for food delivery
items.description: Both require 본인인증 (identity verification tied to postpaid plan). Now that you have postpaid, these are available.
tips: Baemin (배달의민족) is the dominant app. Coupang Eats is growing and often cheaper.
